history.summary: IDENTITY FLAG: 'Shirdi Sai Baba Temple, Faridabad' is an ambiguous label. This file documents the Sector 16A temple (51, Sector 16 Rd), which runs its own website (saibabamandir16a.com) and is described by travel listings as a 3-acre temple with a white marble Sai idol of about 5.5 feet plus Dwarakamai and Dhuni shrines. Faridabad's other prominent Sai institution is Sai Dham - the Shirdi Sai Baba Temple Society at Sector 86, Tigaon Road (established 1988, a major charitable trust running schools, dispensaries and mass marriages); some listing sites appear to conflate the two. Founding details of the Sector 16A temple were not found in published sources (UNVERIFIED).

town_description: Faridabad is Haryana's largest city and a major industrial hub on Delhi's southeastern edge, part of the Delhi NCR. It was founded in 1607 by Shaikh Farid (Mughal emperor Jahangir's treasurer) as Farid's town. Sector 16 is a residential sector in the older part of the city near the Delhi border.

travel.railway: Faridabad Railway Station - about 2-4 km (verify); metro connectivity via Violet Line.
travel.road: 51, Sector 16 Rd, Sector 16A, Faridabad, Haryana; reachable by auto, taxi and city buses (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Thursday evenings are the most popular visiting time for Sai devotees.
visitor_information.opening_hours: UNVERIFIED: hours for the Sector 16A temple were not published in the sources consulted (the Sai Dham Sector 86 society lists 5 AM-9 PM - do not confuse the two). Verify on arrival.
